Hi all — technical details below. I’ve also attached a sample manifest (sample-manifest.txt) and a small example bundle layout.

Canonical fields we capture in the admin-action ledger (all timestamps in UTC ISO8601):
- timestamp
- actor_id (internal user id) and actor_email (if available)
- action_type (e.g., CREATE_MODEL, UPDATE_POLICY, GRANT_ROLE, DELETE_API_KEY)
- target_resource (resource path / model id / project id)
- request_id (globally unique request GUID)
- session_id
- source_ip / source_geo (if resolvable)
- user_agent
- outcome (SUCCESS / FAILURE)
- operator_role (role snapshot at time of action)
- change_blob (JSON diff for config changes; base64-encoded when binary)
- kv_cache_events (when operator touches runtime cache keys)
- tokenized_kv_refs (hashed pointers, not raw tokens)
- request_hash and response_hash (SHA256)

Retention and export:
- Default retention for admin ledger: 365 days. Enterprise customers can extend to 3 years on contract.
- Exports supported: newline-delimited JSON (JSONL) gzipped, Apache Parquet (columnar), and plain CSV for scoped slices.
- Incremental export modes: we support (a) full time-window snapshot, (b) incremental deltas (since last_manifest_version) and (c) streaming export to customer S3 with periodic manifests.

Redaction & pseudonymization:
- Field-level redaction: PII (email, IP) can be redacted or replaced with deterministic pseudonyms for attested review while preserving referential integrity.
- Redaction strategy options: redact-in-export (server-side replacement at export time) or tokenization (retain mapping under customer KMS). Note: removing actor_email entirely will reduce traceability — pseudonymization preferred for audit use cases.

Integrity & attestation:
- Every export bundle includes: a manifest.jsonl, a manifest.sha256 (bundle-level hash list), and a manifest.hmac (HMAC-SHA256).
- We can sign manifests with either Redwood's signing key (X.509) or accept a customer-provided HMAC key for detached HMACs.
- For higher forensic assurance we can produce a notarized attest.txt signed by our Compliance lead (PDF attach) describing extraction parameters.

Operational lead times & SLAs: 
- Standard on-demand one-off extraction: 3-5 business days for scoped windows up to 30 days (no PII redaction).
- PII redaction or pseudonymization adds 2 business days (depending on volume).
- Large historical pulls (>90 days) or full-tenant exports require scheduling (typically 7-14 business days) and may incur time&material costs. Procurement — I'll add an estimate once Marissa confirms the final scope.

Delivery channels:
- Secure S3 push (recommended) with temporary creds
- SFTP with signed manifest
- Encrypted transfer via direct customer VPN on request

Related artifacts: sample-manifest.txt (attached), reference JIRA INF-4921 for the ops runbook to perform an attested extraction.

Ben Carter
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: sample-manifest.txt
